title: Stalk of a pro-etale sheaf at a geometric point
statement:
Let $Y$ be a scheme, $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ its small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to Y$ a geometric point [def-weil-geometric-point]. A *pointed neighbourhood* of $\bar y$ is a pair $(U,\bar u)$ of an object $U\to Y$ of $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ (a weakly étale morphism [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]) and a morphism $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ over $Y$ lifting $\bar y$; a morphism $(U,\bar u)\to(U',\bar u')$ is a morphism $U\to U'$ over $Y$ carrying $\bar u$ to $\bar u'$. For a sheaf $\mathcal F$ (of sets, or of modules) on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$, its *stalk* at $\bar y$ is the colimit

$$
 \mathcal F_{\bar y}=\varinjlim_{(U,\bar u)}\mathcal F(U)
$$

over the opposite of the category of pointed neighbourhoods of $\bar y$; this index category is filtered, because fibre products $U\times_YU'$ and equalizers of pairs of maps of pointed neighbourhoods are again pointed neighbourhoods (morphisms between weakly étale $Y$-schemes are weakly étale).
